title: Mammals of Kruger National Park: combined species list
inclusion: Species on the 2011 SANParks Kruger mammal checklist (Wayback copy), after the owner decisions of 13 Nov 2026 (see docs/BRIEF.md and docs/SOURCES.md). Each family file under data/species/ holds the full evidence.

remaps.note: The 2011 checklist prints the name as Calcochloris obtrusirostris. An iNaturalist taxa search for that spelling returned 0 results. A search for Calcochloris obtusirostris matches species Calcochloris obtusirostris (taxon 42519, preferred_common_name Yellow Golden Mole), which lists Chrysochloris obtusirostris as an invalid scientific name. The stored latin value is the iNaturalist spelling. This is treated as a typographic typo on the PDF (obtrusirostris vs obtusirostris), not as a taxonomic split.

notes: On the official 2011 checklist, but absent from the iNaturalist place 69020 Chrysochloridae taxonomy tree (no observations of any grade). Observation total_results for taxon 42519 in the place is 0.

remaps.note: This is a recorded split, not a simple synonym. iNaturalist still treats Felis silvestris (taxon 922459) as an active species, preferred_common_name European Wildcat. The 2011 checklist already prints (=F. lybica) under Felis silvestris. Place 69020 research-grade African wild-cat observations are identified as Felis lybica (taxon 371414, preferred_common_name African Wildcat, 123); F. silvestris does not appear in the place Felidae taxonomy tree. The F. lybica species name list does not include Felis silvestris, or the trinomial Felis silvestris lybica, as a scientific name (its invalid scientific names are Felis lybicus, Felis ocreata, Felis cafra and Felis haussa). The trinomial Felis silvestris cafra is listed as an invalid scientific name of the subspecies Felis lybica cafra (taxon 922462, preferred_common_name Southern African Wildcat), which has 67 observations of any grade in the place tree. The Kruger taxon is stored as the species Felis lybica because that is the iNaturalist species whose preferred common name is African Wildcat, which has the Kruger records, and which the 2011 list already synonymises as F. lybica.

An iNaturalist taxa search for the 2011 name matches Macronycteris commersonii (taxon 851027, preferred_common_name Commerson's Leaf-nosed Bat), which lists Hipposideros commersoni, Hipposideros commersonii, and Macronycteris commersoni as invalid scientific names. Macronycteris vittata (taxon 851017, preferred_common_name Striped leaf-nosed bat) is a separate active species; its name list does not include Hipposideros commersoni (invalid names are Macronycteris vittatus, Hipposideros vittatus, and Hipposideros marungensis). Observation total_results is 0 for both M. commersonii and M. vittata. Because it is unclear which of those taxa, if either, occurs in Kruger, and there are no Kruger records to decide it, the stored latin value is the 2011 name rather than a guessed remap.
